en.askTitle: Put in your own degree, experience, language level and salary to see whether the skilled-professional route or the standard work status fits you
en.runTitle: Taipei to Tokyo in April 2027: a backend engineer on JPY 9.2 million, points table, take-home pay and first-year budget

fields.label: Years of related work experience
fields.value: 7 years as a backend software engineer

en.template: Help me choose between HSP(i)(b) and the standard work status for a move from {from_city} to {to_city} in {move_date}. I am {age}, my degree is {degree}, I have {experience} of related work experience, my JLPT level is {jlpt}, the offered salary is {salary} and my savings are {savings}. Recalculate the points table, the monthly take-home, the move-in costs and the first-year budget with my numbers, show how thin the margins are, and mark anything unconfirmed. Ask before contacting anyone or paying anything.

phases.title: Three colleagues research in parallel: Japan’s points rules and visa process, tax and social insurance, Tokyo rent and move-in costs
phases.note: Official immigration, tax and pension pages plus dated rent listings
phases.judgment: A figure it could not confirm was kept out of the plan: the tax colleague found no official date for the rise of the lump-sum withdrawal cap from 5 to 8 years, and noted that sources claiming April 2026 have no official backing.

phases.title: Build the guide: points worked example, monthly take-home, move-in costs and a first-year budget in yen and Taiwan dollars
phases.note: Recommendation up front, with the margin shown
phases.judgment: It showed how thin the margin is instead of rounding it away: JPY 9.2M sits only 0.2M above the 9.0M salary line, below which her score falls from 80 to 75. The Japanese-language test gives the buffer, and how the agency counts “annual salary” is flagged as unconfirmed.

phases.title: Three rounds of independent review, recomputing every money figure after each edit, then a layout check on narrow screens
phases.judgment: The reviewers caught real mistakes and the guide was corrected before release: the second round found two wording errors (the rent-to-cost ratios were swapped between the two flats, and a rent range started lower than any example listed), and the third round confirmed both fixes and recomputed every figure.

workers: Read Japan’s immigration agency pages on the skilled-professional points table, what the status gives, and the eligibility certificate process
Collected dated Tokyo rent examples near commute lines, initial costs and the official rules on agency fees
Worked out income tax, resident tax, pension and health insurance on a monthly example, plus the lump-sum withdrawal payment if she leaves
First independent check: recomputed every money figure and compared the claims with the source list
Second independent check after the guide was edited; found two wording errors
Third independent check after the last edit; confirmed the fixes and recomputed every figure
